candidates.existing: Free DGI online platform (filing requires NIFONLINE validation). MDG Services offers a paid done-for-you filing. A user guide circulates on Scribd. No software for managing a register across many clients seen.
candidates.name: RCBE (beneficial-owner register) filing and update service for SMEs, associations, cooperatives and NGOs
candidates.trigger: Beneficial-ownership obligation introduced by the 2024 finance law. DGI platform launched about 16 Jun 2026. Declare within 30 days of incorporation, update on every change, keep a special register, possible DGI audits. Deadline for existing entities not yet communicated. Decree or article not found.
candidates.trigger_note: Close to K03 only by buyer group (accounting firms).
candidates.unchecked: The legal text and decree. The deadline for existing entities and the penalties. Whether the DGI platform supports bulk or accountant filing. How many entities must file. Whether it is a one-off wave or a recurring duty. Not a dedicated local-language competitor search beyond the one run (RCBE logiciel plateforme cabinet).

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: OMH regulates downstream (Loi 99-010, Decree 2004-669/670); 341 stations spread over 4 main distributors, so the buyer group is concentrated. Spring 2026 shortage measures (15 L container limit). No station-level periodic report found. LPG retailers fall under the same OMH licence regime; no retailer-specific rule found.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Clove exporters need an annual MIC agrément (window 1-15 Sept; 108 approved for 2024-25: 38 industrial, 70 artisan) under Decree 88-070. No collector card regime found. Coffee/cocoa EUDR is known (K07). Related to K02.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: CSBF Circular 001/2018 requires electronic tele-declaration within 15 days of period close. MFIs also report monthly to the Microfinance Risk Center (Instruction 002-DCR/09). Likely covered by core-banking vendors. OTIV and current CECAM rules not found.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: No clinic or lab licensing text or insurer-billing scheme found; the CMU is still being rolled out. The Moroccan clinic-billing result was discarded as the wrong country. Nothing usable.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Depots are licensed by the DPLMT and are a temporary measure, with sales limited to essential medicines. A June 2026 bill to allow depots next to pharmacies was opposed by the pharmacists' Order and adjourned (K05 area). Narcotics are governed by Loi 97-039; register duties not read. About 340 pharmacies. No wholesaler rules found.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: The DCAF study says private security is not specifically regulated (date unknown). Private placement agencies are officially prohibited (Labour Minister, July 2025; ILO C181 ratified by Loi 2018-034). Cleaning: nothing found. No candidate.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: The BCMM clean-up plan was approved on 27 Jan 2026. New mining permits resumed for non-gold minerals (first come, first served, at the Ivato Mining Business Center, with 12 regional offices), and the gold moratorium stays. No construction or local-content rule found.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: SAMIFIN lists real-estate agencies, notaries, lawyers and bailiffs as reporting entities (L'Express, June 2025) and says no real-estate suspicious-transaction reports had been filed. The legal text and any reporting portal were not found. Egmont accession is pending.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Police-form checks are by local gendarmerie (Ambilobe 2024). The 2001 star and Ravinala classification is being privatised under the new tourism code (adoption unconfirmed). A voluntary guesthouse classification with SGS has run since June 2025 (gite.mg). Tourist tax is set locally. About 700 establishments (older figure). No software gap clearly proven.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Rosewood/ebony (CITES Appendix II): exports have been stopped since about 2015-16, so no legal market. Organic exports reached USD 350M in 2025 and SYMABIO claims traceability. Artisanal fish-collector rules not found. EUDR and vanilla are known (K07, K02). Customs is GasyNet (K06).

coverage.category: 31. Gold comptoirs, gold collectors and artisanal gold groups (country-specific)
coverage.found: Comptoir agréments are issued yearly (resumed 17 Apr 2023). Collectors need a laissez-passer to move gold. Royalties and tax at source are planned with no start date. The Centrale de l'or (COM) is bringing collectors into the legal system (Aug 2026). The BFM buys only from tax-compliant operators.

The DGI platform launched around 16 Jun 2026 (date from a vendor and the press). Private entities are covered: companies, cooperatives, associations, NGOs, foundations and GIEs. Threshold is 25% (5% for mining). Declare within 30 days of incorporation, then update on changes and keep a register. Deadline for existing entities not yet announced. Free state platform exists.

coverage.category: 33. E-money distribution agents and mobile-money cash points (country-specific)
coverage.found: Loi 2016-056 on e-money; CSBF Instruction 002/2018 on agents (mandate contracts, controls, AML). Compliance sits with the operators (Mvola, Orange Money, Airtel), not the agents. A 0.5% transfer-tax bill was proposed in Nov 2024; outcome unknown.

Private teachers need an authorisation to teach to get State allowances (ONEP, 2026). No school-level periodic report found. Private universities were inspected and found partly non-conforming (Apr 2026).

coverage.category: 35. Tour operators, travel agencies and tourist guides (country-specific)
coverage.found: Loi 95-017 on tourism; more than 650 licensed guides; the guide licensing process restarted after a gap since 2019. No current licence-renewal or reporting rule found.

coverage.category: 36. LFI 2026 and e-invoicing changes for SMEs (country-specific)
coverage.found: Decree of 2 Jul 2025 makes e-invoicing mandatory for B2B and B2G, phased by size, six months after the central platform launches. LFI 2026: IR-without-VAT option for 200-400M Ar turnover (needs certified accounts); rent deductible only with a lease and invoices; non-profit rate 10% to 20%. Overlaps K01.

coverage.category: 37. Small-scale mining permit holders (PREA) and gemstone collectors (country-specific)
coverage.found: The permit reopening in 2026 creates a wave of applicants and permit holders. No gem-collector declaration forms were found.
